entities.summary:
Jan Rzeszowski (died 1488-03-08) was a prominent Polish nobleman, soldier, and clergyman who served as the Bishop of Kraków from 1471 until his death. His episcopate marked a period of significant ecclesiastical and political influence within the Kingdom of Poland, situated at the heart of the powerful Jagiellonian dynasty's reign. As head of one of the wealthiest and most prestigious dioceses in Central Europe, Rzeszowski played a crucial role in the spiritual administration and temporal affairs of the realm, particularly during the later years of King Casimir IV Jagiellon's rule, a monarch deeply engaged in both regional and international power struggles.

During his seventeen-year tenure, Bishop Rzeszowski oversaw the spiritual life and considerable material assets of the Kraków diocese, which included the venerable Wawel Cathedral and the burgeoning Jagiellonian University. His episcopacy coincided with the Polish–Hungarian War (1471–1479), a conflict over the Bohemian throne, where he would have been expected to provide political and financial support to King Casimir IV. While specific records of his personal military involvement are sparse for this period, his earlier background as a soldier suggests a pragmatic understanding of the era's martial demands. He also likely engaged in the patronage of religious art and architecture, typical for a prelate of his standing, contributing to the cultural flourishing associated with the Jagiellonian Golden Age.
